answer: Bandwidth-Weighted Inference Bottleneck. Nodes route requests based on verified TCP throughput, preventing cheap virtual spawns. An attacker spinning up thousands of virtual machines hits a sharp cost mesa because acquiring distinct physical connections requires capital expenditure per node. Much like subterranean water carves a karst landscape by dissolving rock under pressure, continuous cryptographic verification erodes the profitability of low-tier duplicates. If throughput drops below baseline, system rewards route elsewhere like a falcon diving past stationary targets.
